house.description: Commissioner directed to approve youth skills training programs in construction trades.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Workforce, Labor, and Economic Development Finance and Policy
Authors added Engen, Zeleznikar and Johnson, W.

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to workforce development; directing the commissioner to approve youth skills training programs in the construction trades; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 175.46, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 175.46, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 3a.+]

[+Construction trades programs.+]

[+The commissioner must: +]

[+(1) approve youth skills training programs in the construction trades, if the program is restricted to work at a central location such as a headquarters site or training facility; and +]

[+(2) exempt students in programs under this subdivision from any conflicting child labor laws, as allowed under section 181A.07, subdivision 7. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to workforce development; directing the commissioner to approve youth skills training programs in the construction trades; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 175.46, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 175.46, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 3a.

Construction trades programs.

The commissioner must:

(1) approve youth skills training programs in the construction trades, if the program is restricted to work at a central location such as a headquarters site or training facility; and

(2) exempt students in programs under this subdivision from any conflicting child labor laws, as allowed under section 181A.07, subdivision 7.
additions: (1) approve youth skills training programs in the construction trades, if the program is restricted to work at a central location such as a headquarters site or training facility; and
(2) exempt students in programs under this subdivision from any conflicting child labor laws, as allowed under section 181A.07, subdivision 7.
